description:
File: crates/core/src/util.rs
Lines: 71-78

Finding: is_loopback_addr() uses rsplit_once(':') to split host from port. For a bare IPv6 address without brackets and without a port (e.g. '::1'), rsplit_once(':') splits on the last colon, yielding host='' and port='1'. The empty string fails IP parse and is not 'localhost', so the function returns false instead of true.

For IPv4 without a port (e.g. '127.0.0.1'), rsplit_once returns None so unwrap_or(addr) gives '127.0.0.1', which parses correctly as loopback. IPv4 is safe.

Impact: Any caller passing a bare '::1' (no port, no brackets) gets a wrong non-loopback result. In practice, TOML listen.addr values are 'host:port' strings, so this edge case would only arise if someone writes '::1' without a port in their config. The OS would reject such a string in TcpListener::bind anyway, but the guard would also incorrectly report non-loopback if evaluated beforehand. Test coverage gap: the test suite tests '[::1]:9090' but not bare '::1'.

Fix: Before rsplit_once, check if addr starts with '[' to distinguish bracketed IPv6 from bare IPv6. Or, use addr.parse::<std::net::SocketAddr>() first and fall back to host-split only if that fails.
title: is_loopback_addr: bare ::1 (no port) returns false
